findings.section: src/esa_core.py clip_intervals (line 618) as used by vor_corrected_event_wise (lines 660, 672); protocol endpoints.E4_vor_corrected_event_wise
findings.issue: clip_intervals keeps only intervals with e2 > s2, so zero-length (point) event segments are dropped from the merged event union that decides FPe. An alarm that overlaps only a point event is then counted as a true positive for the event and as a false positive at the same time, contradicting the protocol's 'FPe = episodes overlapping no included event and no excluded event'. The test labels contain 108 zero-length rows in test events, three zero-duration test events (id_118, id_42, id_55) and 26 zero-length rows in five events (id_118, id_183, id_186, id_187, id_189) that no positive-length test-event segment covers.
findings.evidence: Toy test: alarms [150,250],[300,350],[690,710],[900,950] s against events [100,200], [400,450] (rare) and a point at 700 s returned TPe 2, FNe 1, FPe 3, Pre 0.32; with the one-line fix FPe 2, Pre 0.40 as expected. Data counts from f3_schema/meta_labels.csv and meta_anomaly_types.csv.
findings.required_change: In esa_core.clip_intervals replace 'keep = e2 > s2' with 'keep = e2 >= s2'. Alarm spans are never zero-length, so alarm durations, FPt and Nt are unchanged; only the FPe status of alarms overlapping a point event changes. Re-run PT1 is not needed (evaluation-only function).

findings.section: src/esa_arm.py unit_eval, ep_rows_all accumulation (lines 1082-1093) and atomic_csv(outs[6], pd.DataFrame(ep_rows_all)) (line 1136)
findings.issue: Episode rows of all six models are accumulated as Python dicts with 27 keys each before one DataFrame is built. Measured on this interpreter: 300,000 such rows occupy 620 MB, with an 808 MB peak during the DataFrame conversion. The protocol anticipates more than 20,000 episodes per model (the cap), so six models can reach 120,000-300,000 rows and push the eval unit past the 700 MB floor on a host with 1.5-2 GB available. The eval unit carries no freeze gate, so a post-freeze patch would run under a code hash that differs from the freeze record.
findings.evidence: tracemalloc measurement in the reviewer's scratch script; Config.min_available_mb = 700; progress.jsonl shows 1.38-1.52 GB available during the pre-freeze prep units.
findings.required_change: In unit_eval keep a per-model list: after the 'for k in range(n_ep)' loop append pd.DataFrame(model_rows) to a list ep_frames (model_rows being that model's rows), and at write time use pd.concat(ep_frames, ignore_index=True) (or an empty frame when the list is empty) in place of pd.DataFrame(ep_rows_all). Output bytes are unchanged. Apply before the freeze so that no post-freeze code change is needed.

findings.section: protocol endpoints.E4 (window AUROC/AP) and secondary_prespecified_descriptive.S_L_lightweight; esa_arm.unit_eval lines 1005-1006
findings.issue: Window AUROC/AP uses positives = valid test windows overlapping a scoreable event and negatives = every other valid test window not overlapping a gap. In the six-channel refit, windows of the 26 test events that touch no lightweight channel are non-scoreable and therefore count as negatives, whereas the false-alarm rule excludes them from nominal time. For the primary set every test event is scoreable, so only S_L is affected. Descriptive; the protocol does not state this.
findings.evidence: unit_eval: scoreable = events with m > 0; yw/sw masks; nominal_test = ~labeled_test; F3_FACTS test_lightweight_scoreable_events = 65 of 91.
findings.required_change: Append to endpoints.E4: 'Window AUROC/AP: positives are valid test windows overlapping a scoreable event; negatives are all other valid test windows outside gap segments, which in S_L includes windows of test events that touch no lightweight channel.' No code change.

label_isolation.label_readers: Labels are read at exactly one site, esa_arm.read_segments (grep of src/: labels.csv appears only there and in the property-test table writer). unit_stdz calls it with pre_evaluation=True (segments with StartTime < 2007-01-01, EndTime clipped at 2007-01-01 minus 1 ns); unit_eval calls it with pre_evaluation=False and is the first reader of test rows. unit_prep reads no label; unit_fit, unit_episodes and unit_attr_episode read only meta.npz, scores and episode files derived from stdz.
label_isolation.can_pre_evaluation_depend_on_test_rows: No. The filter removes test rows before any use, and the period masks additionally confine nominal_fit, nominal_val, sup_y and the raw statistics to fit/validation windows and grid times. The artifacts that would change under an unfiltered read are the stored masks in meta.npz (labeled_any_pre, event_any_pre, gap_any_pre) and the pre_evaluation_segments count in stats.json, both covered by PT1.
label_isolation.pt1_meaningfulness: PT1 as run edits only test rows (1,711), covers all six families, episodes and attr_episode artifacts (266 files, hashes only, quarantined) and passed; it detects any read of test rows before the filter and, as a by-product, certifies byte-level run-to-run determinism of every family. It cannot detect a reader that bypasses cfg.labels_csv, which the grep rules out. Its pass is meaningful.

The gate requires status PUBLIC_FREEZE_VERIFIED and equality of the code_sha256 dict with the hashes of every esa_*.py in src/.

summary: v3 implements all sixteen F1 changes; the five declared deviations are justified. The code matches v3 and the synthetic core in every decision-critical definition I could test (features, standardization guard, threshold, episodes, tau and window weights, aggregated masses, cap, AUROC, bootstrap bounds, assay gate, decision rule, VOR quantities), label isolation holds with a single filtered reader, the freeze gate blocks every scoring path, and the pre-freeze evidence carries over to the path-only refactored src/. One blocking defect: vor_corrected_event_wise drops zero-length event segments, so alarms on point events count as false positives (one-line fix). One memory risk in the eval unit and three wording or provenance notes. Freeze after applying D-01.
